sections.html:
Collector and assessor both work from the county building on the West Plains square, 35 Court Square. The County Collector is in Room 201, phone (417) 256-4001, fax (417) 257-0090. The counter is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 am until 4:30 pm, noon hour included, and shuts for state holidays.

The assessor is in Suite 202 at (417) 256-8284 and opens at 8:00 am. The assessor's site offers GIS mapping and a subscription parcel search at howell.missouriassessors.com. The collector does more than houses: it prepares separate statements for personal property such as cars, trucks and boats, for real estate, and for utilities such as railroads and gas lines, and it issues merchant licenses.

sections.h2: Paying your Howell County tax bill
sections.html:
Mailing starts in November, and each statement is due when it arrives. Delinquency begins after December 31, and a check postmarked January 1 or later is returned unless late fees are included. A statement that never turns up still leaves the tax owing, so phone the office if one has not come by the end of November.

Ways to pay Howell County property tax
MethodHow it works
OnlineClick Pay Taxes on the collector's site
Phone1-800-652-0405, current taxes only; enter county number 18 and the PIN from your statement
MailPostmarked no later than December 31
Drop boxOutside the Howell County Office Building
CounterRoom 201, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm

Each month the collector passes what it has taken in to the taxing entities that levy against your parcel.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax if you sell or move mid-year
sections.html:
Under RSMo 137.075, liability attaches to whoever holds property on January 1, even a buyer who closes that same day. A person who moves out of Missouri in June still owes tax for that whole year. The law gives no proration.

That rule is written mostly around vehicles and other personal property, which owners list with the assessor before March 1. A house works differently in practice. What you and the buyer each pay of the year's real estate bill comes from the sale contract and settlement statement, so read the proration clause first.

sections.h2: What share of a home's value is taxed
sections.html:
Homes are taxed on 19 percent of true value, farmland on 12 and commercial property on 32, as set in RSMo 137.115. Values are reset every odd year.

  • Any raise over 15 percent on a home, unless new building caused it, calls for an on-site inspection.
  • You may ask the inspector to come inside, and the notice must give you thirty days to do so.
  • On appeal, RSMo 138.060 makes the assessor prove a raise of that size is justified.

Open your parcel record on the assessor's site before you call so you can quote the parcel number. The subscription search there also shows what nearby properties are carried at, which is useful when you want to compare your value with a neighbor's.

sections.h2: Your options if the number looks wrong
sections.html:
Begin with the Board of Equalization, which takes filings until the second Monday in July. The State Tax Commission is the next level and allows 30 days from the date of the Board's letter. A stipulation signed with the assessor ends the case permanently.

Paying under protest is a separate tool. RSMo 139.031 asks for the whole bill before delinquency, a written explanation filed with the collector and a lawsuit against the collector within ninety days. The collector holds the contested share in its own fund while the case runs. A tax paid by mistake can be credited or refunded if the taxpayer applies within three years.

The collector holds the sale on the fourth Monday in August, and RSMo 140.150 agrees. Until the gavel falls, an owner can settle by paying the tax, penalty, interest and costs. The collector mails notice to the record owner, though a letter that goes astray does not wipe out the debt.

If you owe a balance, ask (417) 256-4001 for a payoff so the title company can pay it out of your proceeds.

sections.h2: Howell County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Along the Arkansas line, Howell County is led by West Plains. It has an estimated 40,798 people and 18,288 housing units, and 70.3 percent of homes are lived in by owners. Expect a median owned-home value of $173,000 and median rent of $733. Owner costs average $1,109 with a mortgage and $394 without. With only 67 permits issued in 2025, buyers mostly choose from existing houses.

Other towns include Brandsville, Mountain View and Willow Springs.

The collector issues separate statements for personal property, real estate and utilities, and a homeowner usually sees two of them. The real estate statement covers the house and land. The personal property statement covers vehicles, boats and similar items that you listed with the assessor before March 1, so a seller who owns a truck or boat should expect a second envelope.

Each kind can be delinquent on its own. When you ask for a payoff, say clearly that you want every statement tied to your name, then ask whether the amount includes late fees. The phone line at 1-800-652-0405 handles current taxes only, so an older balance has to be paid at the counter or by another route.

sections.h2: A practical checklist for the week before closing
sections.html:
1. Confirm with Room 201 that the real estate statement for the year is paid or that the payoff is known.
  2. Ask whether any personal property statement is open under your name.
  3. Print the parcel record from the assessor's site and compare it with the deed.
  4. Give the title company the payoff, the parcel number and the contract's proration clause.
  5. Keep the receipt and put it with the settlement statement.

A drop box outside the county building takes payments after hours, and a check in the mail must carry a postmark no later than December 31 to count as timely.

sections.h2: Selling a Howell County house with taxes due
sections.html:
Start with a statement from Room 201 and a call to (417) 256-4001 to see whether an earlier year is open. Ask for a payoff figure and give it to the title company, along with the parcel number from the assessor's site. Keep the receipt with your closing papers.

Remember that the year's bill is assigned by your contract, not by the county. If a lien, a tenant or a repair list is slowing a normal sale, a cash buyer can close without a lender's appraisal and the title company pays the county balance from your proceeds.

faqs.q: What phone number pays a Howell County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call 1-800-652-0405 for current taxes. Enter county number 18, then the PIN printed on your statement. Back taxes cannot be paid on that line.

faqs.q: Who is the Howell County assessor's office?
faqs.a: It is in Suite 202 at 35 Court Square, West Plains, open weekdays from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm. The phone is (417) 256-8284.

faqs.q: When must personal property be listed in Howell County?
faqs.a: Before March 1 each year. Property is assessed as it stood on January 1.

faqs.q: Is tax prorated if I leave Missouri?
faqs.a: No, the tax rests on what you held on January 1, and the law has no proration. A home sale contract can still split that year's real estate bill between buyer and seller.

faqs.q: Where can I check my parcel before an appeal?
faqs.a: Use the assessor's site, howell.missouriassessors.com, or call (417) 256-8284. Have the parcel number ready, and file any Board of Equalization appeal by the second Monday in July.
